results.title: Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) Root Zone and Surface Wetness for Hurricane Nolo
results.description:
Dates of Images:

September 22, 2026, September 23, 2026, September 24, 2026, September 25, 2026, September 27, 2026

Date of Next Image:

Unknown; data available daily with a 2 to 3 day latency.

Summary:

SMAP Level-4 (L4) surface and root zone soil moisture (L4_SM) data are provided in three products. The SMAP L4 Global 3-hourly 9 km EASE-Grid Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture Geophysical Data (SPL4SMGP, DOI: 10.5067/T5RUATAQREF8) product is a series of 3-hourly time average geophysical land surface fields that are output by the L4_SM algorithm. It is likely of primary interest to most users. The SMAP L4 Global 3-hourly 9 km EASE-Grid Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture Analysis Update (SPL4SMAU, DOI: 10.5067/02LGW4DGJYRX) product provides diagnostics from the land surface analysis updates. It consists of a series of 3-hourly instantaneous (or snapshot) files that contain the assimilated SMAP observations, the corresponding land model predictions and analysis estimates, and additional data assimilation diagnostics. Lastly, the SMAP L4 Global 9 km EASE-Grid Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture Land Model Constants (SPL4SMLM, DOI: 10.5067/PXQIBL2ALDZD) product provides static (time-invariant) land surface model constants that will be needed by some users for further interpretation of the geophysical land surface fields. This product consists of only one granule (file) per L4_SM data product version (as defined by a distinct Science Version ID). For each product, SMAP L-band brightness temperature data from descending and ascending half-orbit satellite passes (approximately 6:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. local solar time, respectively) are assimilated into a land surface model that is gridded using an Earth-fixed, global cylindrical 9 km Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid, Version 2.0 (EASE-Grid 2.0) projection.

Suggested Usage

Parameters

  1. Surface Wetness - Shows moisture in the top 5 cm of soil. Good for flash flooding risk from rain. 

  2. Root Zone Wetness - Shows moisture in the top 1 m of soil. Good for longer term monitoring of water basin height and potential riverine flooding risk.

Both parameters are dimensionless "Soil wetness units" that represent a ratio of volume of water to volume of space available on a 0-1 scale. From documentation: “Soil wetness units (dimensionless) vary between 0 and 1 (dimensionless) and indicate relative saturation between completely dry conditions and completely saturated conditions, respectively.”

Platform(s):

GEOS-5SMAP

Sensor(s):

  • NOT APPLICABLE (root zone)

  • SMAP L-BAND RADIOMETER (surface soil moisture)

Data Format(s):

GeoTIFF

Temporal Resolution:

3 hour

Spatial Resolution:

9 km

Spatial Reference System(s):

WGS 84 / NSIDC EASE-Grid 2.0 Global

EPSG:6933

Credits:

Funding was provided by the NASA SMAP Mission. Computational resources were provided by the NASA High-End Computing program through the NASA Center for Climate Simulation. The generation and dissemination of SMAP data products possible includes staff at GSFC, JPL, and NSIDC.

results.title: Tropical Storms Web Map
results.description:
The following layers are featured in this map:
  • Recent Hurricanes, Cyclones, and Typhoons Observed Track, Position, and Wind Swath: Provided by NOAA, the National Hurricane Center, and Esri these layers display the distribution of recent events. Wind swath is not automatically enabled but may be toggled on using the layers widget. ( https://services9.arcgis.com/RHVPKKiFTONKtxq3/arcgis/rest/services/Recent_Hurricanes_v1/FeatureServer )
  • GPM_NRT_30min_Latest: This layer is the most recent available precipitation rate from the Integrated Multi-Satellite Retrieval for Global Precipitation Measurement (IMERG) Early run. With 30 minute temporal resolution, this layer provides precipitation rate in millimeters per hour in Near Real-Time. ( https://maps.disasters.nasa.gov/ags03/rest/services/NRT_Latest/GPM_NRT_30min_Latest/ImageServer ) For the full collection of GPM IMERG Early Precipitation Rate, see the service   here   (  https://arcgis.gesdisc.eosdis.nasa.gov/authoritative/rest/services/GPM_3IMERGHHE_06/ImageServer) 
  • Popgrid counts: Gridded Population of the World, Version 4 (GPWv4): Population Density contains layers for several years showing population density estimates (persons/square kilometer). ( https://ciesin.columbia.edu/arcgis/rest/services/ciesin/popgrid_counts/MapServer )
  • SMAP Soil Moisture Anomaly: Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) data and surface soil moisture models which depict the deviation of soil moisture from an average based on the 2-layer modified Palmer Hydrologic Model. ( https://maps.disasters.nasa.gov/ags03/rest/services/NRT/smap_soilmoisture_anomaly/ImageServer )
  • analysis_ocean_sfc_sst_time: This layer, displaying ocean surface temperature is important for monitoring conditions that lead to tropical storm formation. Provided by the NOAA ( National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration )/NWS (National Weather Service)/NCEP (National Centers for Environmental Protection) operational Near-Sea Surface Temperature (NSST) analysis and the NASA/SPoRT experimental North American Sea Surface Temperature Composite, Sea Surface Temperature is shown in degrees Fahrenheit. ( nowcoast/analysis_ocean_sfc_sst_time (MapServer) (noaa.gov) )
  • VIIRS Day/Night: The VIIRS layer in this map showcase both the Near Real-Time (NRT) and event based capabilities of NASA GIS data. The VIIRS layer is NRT color imagery. ( VIIRS (ImageServer) (arcgis.com) )
results.snippet: Near Real-Time monitoring of tropical storm formation and effects.

results.title: Drought Web Map
results.description:
• Vegetation - Surface Reflectance: The web app's basemap (Figure 2) has a live updated visualization based on Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) imagery with a band combination that highlights changes in vegetation. Cloud cover is white, vegetation is green, and sediment is pink. The spatial resolution is 250m, the band combination is 1-2-1 (Visible red and Short Wave Near Infrared), and the service is updated daily. The service is available on NASA ArcGIS Online (AGOL) and through this url (https://modis.arcgis.com/arcgis/rest/services/MODIS/ImageServer) and more information on the layer can be found here ( Vegetation - Surface Reflectance (MODIS / Terra) - Overview (arcgis.com) ). The MODIS instrument is on board the Terra satellite.

  • Evaporative Stress Index (NASA SERVIR): Figure 7 shows a layer portraying regions of drought where vegetation is stressed due to lack of water. It is updated weekly and has a 5km spatial resolution. Green represents areas with adequate soil moisture. Yellow and red represent areas that are stressed. The sensors used to produce this layer are Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership (NPP), Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), Special Sensor Microwave Imager (SSMI), SSMI Sounder (SSMIS), Windsat, Global Change Observation Mission-Water (GCOM-W1, GCOM-W2) funded by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, FY-3B (Feng-Yun 3B from the China Meteorological Administration and the National Remote Sensing Center of China), GPM Core. Not only does this layer indicate regions experiencing drought, but could help predict which areas are at risk of drought. The layer and metadata are available at  Global/ESI_4WK (MapServer) (servirglobal.net) .

  • The Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) Near Real Time (NRT) 30-Minute Precipitation Accumulation Latest Image: Figure 6 shows millimeters of accumulated precipitation, based on the Integrated Multi SatellitE Retrievals for Global Precipitation Measurement (IMERG) algorithm Early run product. Precipitation could be helpful in determining which areas are at risk for flooding or drought. Green indicates areas of low precipitation, and yellow, moderate precipitation, while red indicates areas of highest precipitation. The service (https://maps.disasters.nasa.gov/ags03/rest/services/NRT_Latest/GPM_NRT_30min_Latest/ImageServer) is updated throughout the day to show the most up to date precipitation values. The spatial resolution is 0.1 degrees. For the full collection of GPM IMERG Early Precipitation Rate, see the service  here  ( https://arcgis.gesdisc.eosdis.nasa.gov/authoritative/rest/services/GPM_3IMERGHHE_06/ImageServer)

  • Soil Moisture Anomaly 3-Day Composite: The layer in Figure 5 is based on Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) data and surface soil moisture models to depict the deviation of soil moisture from an average based on the 2-layer modified Palmer Hydrologic Model. Spatial resolution is 0.25 degrees. Dark red areas depict negative variations, indicating a lack of soil moisture compared to average. Blue and purple regions represent positive anomalies, indication a higher soil moisture than average. A lack of soil moisture could indicate a drought while one explanation of a positive anomaly is a flood. (https://maps.disasters.nasa.gov/ags03/rest/services/NRT/smap_soilmoisture_anomaly/ImageServer).

  • Landsat 8 Imagery Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) Colorized: The layer displayed in Figure 4 is updated daily to show the NDVI using Landsat 8 bands. NDVI can be used to indicate the density and type of vegetation cover. This layer is created by Esri and is available through the following URL (https://landsat2.arcgis.com/arcgis/rest/services/Landsat8_Views/ImageServer).

  • The Gridded Population of the World, Version 4 (GPWv4): Population Density (Figure 3) contains global 2020 population density estimates (persons/square kilometer) to assist in determining the number of people that could be affected by drought. GPWv4 contains layers for several years, however the 2020 layer was selected to be visible to most closely reflect the time portrayed in the other layers. Areas with higher populations are shown in orange and red. The service may be found at the Socioeconomic Data and Applications Center (SEDAC) endpoint here ( ciesin/popgrid_counts (MapServer) (columbia.edu) ).
results.snippet: A web map including layers useful for monitoring drought conditions.

results.title: Daily Global Landslide Exposure Map
results.description:
Landslides are a widespread and often underestimated natural hazard, causing thousands of deaths and significant economic damage each year. They routinely block roads, destroy infrastructure, and disrupt communities worldwide. While intense or prolonged rainfall is the most common landslide trigger, earthquakes and human activities can also cause them.

The global Landslide Hazard Assessment for Situational Awareness (LHASA) model provides users with a comprehensive view of landslide hazard in near real-time. Using machine learning, LHASA combines rainfall data from the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) satellite with antecedent soil moisture from the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) satellite to identify areas currently at risk from landslides. The model shows where and when landslides are most probable, then calculates the exposed population and road length within each administrative district, helping users understand both the hazard and potential impacts on communities and infrastructure.

Daily global landslide exposure assessment from the LHASA (Landslide Hazard Assessment for Situational Awareness) model. Color-coded hazard levels range from red (very high exposure) to yellow (low exposure), helping users identify areas where landslides may occur.

To learn more please visit: https://landslides.nasa.gov/

Summary:
Landslides are a widespread and often underestimated natural hazard, causing thousands of deaths and significant economic damage each year. They routinely block roads, destroy infrastructure, and disrupt communities worldwide. Using machine learning, LHASA combines rainfall data from the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) satellite with antecedent soil moisture from the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) satellite to identify areas currently at risk from landslides.
